question: 落叶，一定要归根吗？
question_en: Must the falling leaf return to its roots?
sub: 想回去的，是那些人，还是一段回不去的时光？
sub_en: Is it the people you want to go back to, or a time you can never return to?

casting.reason: 他写过中国现代文学里最著名的一次返乡：回去卖掉老屋，发现故乡和闰土都已陌生，最后把母亲接出了故土。
casting.reason_en: He wrote the most famous homecoming in modern Chinese literature: going back to sell the family house, finding both his hometown and his childhood friend estranged, and taking his mother away with him.

casting.reason: 他把「无家可归」看作现代人的命运，主张根在于对一处地方的照料，而非出生地本身。
casting.reason_en: He sees homelessness as the fate of modern people and argues that roots lie in caring for a place, not in where one happens to be born.

casting.reason: 她用实验证明记忆是重建的，提醒人们，脑中的老家未必是真实的老家。
casting.reason_en: Her experiments show that memory is reconstructed, a warning that the hometown in your head may not be the real one.

casting.reason: 她的社会情绪选择理论解释了为什么时间越少，人越想回到最亲的人身边。
casting.reason_en: Her theory of socioemotional selectivity explains why, as time grows short, people want to be near those closest to them.

casting.reason: 他把根落在亲人身上，主张远行可以，心不能远，亲老则当归或托人代侍。
casting.reason_en: He locates the root in one's kin: travelling far is acceptable, but the heart must not drift, and when parents age one should return or arrange for others to care for them.

casting.reason: 他承认望见故乡的畅然，却反对把归乡当成道义，主张先问父母自己想要什么。
casting.reason_en: He admits the gladness of seeing one's old home but rejects treating return as a duty, insisting that you first ask your parents what they actually want.

casting.reason: 他一生自认阿尔及利亚之子，把故乡化成随身的阳光，又始终放不下留在那里的母亲。
casting.reason_en: A lifelong son of Algeria, he turned home into a sunlight he carried with him, yet never stopped being tied to the mother he left there.

casting.reason: 他以缘起与无自性拆解「根」与「归处」的固定性，劝人不执归、也不执不归。
casting.reason_en: With dependent arising and the absence of self-nature, he dismantles the idea of a fixed root or a fixed place to return to, urging people to cling neither to going back nor to staying away.

posts.text: 「我冒了严寒，回到相隔二千余里，别了二十余年的故乡去。」这是我写《故乡》的开头。那一回，是去卖掉老屋、把母亲接走的。少年时的闰土见了我，恭恭敬敬叫一声「老爷」，**我们之间已经隔了一层可悲的厚障壁了**。所以我疑心：许多人想回去的，并不是那块地，而是那个还没被生活磨过的自己。那个，谁也回不去。
posts.text_en: "I braved the bitter cold to travel more than six hundred miles back to the old home I had left over twenty years before." That is how my story "My Old Home" begins. I went back that time to sell the family house and take my mother away. Runtu, my boyhood friend, greeted me with a respectful "Master", **and I knew a lamentably thick wall had grown up between us.** So I suspect that what many people long to go back to is not a piece of land but the self they were before life wore them down. Nobody gets back to that.

posts.text: 你们把「根」想成地图上的一个点，买张车票就能回去。可我说的无家可归，是现代人的命运：人被当作可调配的劳动力四处搬运，住在哪里都只是落脚。**栖居不是占有一个地址，而是对一处地方的照料与守护。**荷尔德林写返乡，返的是对近处的熟悉。回了老家却整天刷手机，照样无家可归。
posts.text_en: You picture "roots" as a dot on the map, reachable with a train ticket. But the homelessness I speak of is the fate of modern people: we are treated as labour to be deployed and shipped from place to place, so that wherever we live we are only passing through. **Dwelling is not owning an address; it is caring for a place and looking after it.** When Hölderlin wrote of homecoming, what he came home to was nearness, the familiar close at hand. Go back to your hometown and spend all day on your phone, and you are just as homeless.

glossary.无家可归: Heimatlosigkeit（无家可归）：海德格尔用语，指现代人与自身所处之地失去了切身联系，不在于有没有住处，而在于哪里都不真正「住」。
glossary.栖居: Wohnen / dwelling（栖居）：海德格尔晚期概念，指人在一处地方安顿下来、爱护它、与它相互归属的方式，而非仅仅占有或使用它。

glossary_en.homelessness: Heidegger's Heimatlosigkeit: the modern loss of any lived bond with the place one is in. It is not about lacking a roof but about never truly dwelling anywhere.
glossary_en.Dwelling: Heidegger's late concept (Wohnen): the way people settle in a place, care for it and come to belong to it, as opposed to merely owning or using it.

posts.text: 先说一条实验室里反复验证的事实：记忆不是录像，是每次回想时重建一遍。重建时，后来听到的话、看过的照片、过年时的心情都会混进去。几十年后你脑中的老家，**是被你自己反复修过图的老家**。所以回去后的失落，一半不是老家变了，而是它本来就不是你记得的样子。这不丢人，只是做决定前，别拿修过图的版本当依据。
posts.text_en: Let me start with something the lab has confirmed again and again: memory is not a recording; it is rebuilt each time you recall it, a process called reconstructive memory. As it is rebuilt, things you heard later, photos you saw, your mood over the holidays all get mixed in. The hometown in your head after decades away **is one you have retouched yourself, many times over.** So half the disappointment of going back is not that the place changed, but that it never quite looked the way you remember. Nothing shameful in that. Just don't base a decision on the retouched version.

glossary.重建: reconstructive memory（重建性记忆）：记忆每次被提取时都会重新组装，容易掺入事后信息、情绪与他人的讲述，因而会随时间漂移。

glossary_en.reconstructive memory: The finding that memories are reassembled each time they are retrieved, so later information, emotion and other people's retellings creep in and the memory drifts over time.

posts.text: 我研究的是：人觉得来日方长，就向外探索；觉得时间不多了，就往回收，守住最亲的几个人。这叫社会情绪选择。所以人到中年、父母到老年，想回去的念头变强，**不是软弱或倒退，而是时间视野收窄后，人在重排优先级**。也算笔账：一年回去一次、住五天，父母再活二十年，剩下的相处就是一百天。算它不为吓人，是让你看清自己在选什么。
posts.text_en: My research shows that when people feel time stretching ahead, they explore outward; when they feel it running short, they pull in and hold on to the few people closest to them. This is socioemotional selectivity. So when you reach middle age and your parents reach old age, the pull to go back grows stronger. **That is not weakness or regression; it is what happens to priorities when your time horizon narrows.** Do the arithmetic, too: visit once a year for five days, and if your parents live another twenty years, you have a hundred days left together. The point is not to frighten you, but to let you see what you are choosing.

glossary.社会情绪选择: socioemotional selectivity（社会情绪选择）：卡斯滕森的理论，认为人对剩余时间的感知决定动机——时间宽裕时追求新知与拓展，时间有限时转向情感意义与亲密关系。
glossary.时间视野: time horizon（时间视野）：一个人主观感到自己还剩多少时间，它比实际年龄更能预测人把精力投向哪里。

glossary_en.socioemotional selectivity: Carstensen's theory that perceived time left shapes motivation: with time to spare people seek novelty and expansion; with time limited they turn to emotional meaning and close ties.
glossary_en.time horizon: How much time a person subjectively feels they have left; it predicts where people invest their energy better than chronological age does.

posts.text: 君子有三乐，父母俱存，兄弟无故，一乐也。乐不在乡土，而在亲在。**根者，亲也，非土也。**然亲之所在，不可不顾。今之人奔走千里以求升斗，岁一归省，匆匆而去，谓之孝乎？吾不责其远游，责其心远。心近，则千里犹比邻；心远，则同屋犹路人。
posts.text_en: A gentleman has three joys, and the first is that his parents are both living and his brothers have come to no harm. The joy lies not in the soil of home but in one's parents still being alive. **The root is your kin, not the land.** Yet wherever your parents are, you cannot leave them unattended. People today travel a thousand miles to scrape a living, visit home once a year and hurry off again. Is that filial? I don't blame them for going far; I blame the heart for drifting. With the heart close, a thousand miles is next door; with it far, people under one roof are strangers.
posts.vernacular: 君子有三种快乐，其中一种是父母都健在、兄弟平安无事。这快乐不在老家那块地，而在亲人还在。**根是亲人，不是土地。**但亲人在哪里，你就不能不管。今天的人奔波千里去挣口饭吃，一年回去看一次，匆匆又走，这叫孝吗？我不怪你走得远，我怪的是心走远了。心近，千里之外也像邻居；心远，住在一个屋里也像陌路人。

glossary.孝: filial piety（孝）：儒家伦理的根基，指子女对父母的奉养、敬重与顾念，孟子尤重其中发自内心的那份亲爱。

glossary_en.filial: Filial piety (xiao), the root of Confucian ethics: a child's care for, respect towards and concern for their parents. Mencius stressed the affection behind it, not just the duties.

posts.text: 旧国旧都，望之畅然；虽使丘陵草木之缗，入之者十九，犹之畅然。**此人之常情，不必讳，亦不必执。**泉涸，鱼相与处于陆，相呴以湿，相濡以沫，不如相忘于江湖。归亦可，不归亦可；所恶者，以归为义，强己而归，归而怨，怨而病。叶落而归根，风也；叶飘而远去，亦风也。
posts.text_en: Gazing on one's old country and old city, one feels a sweep of gladness; even if weeds and hillside growth have swallowed nine-tenths of it, still the gladness comes. **This is plain human feeling: no need to hide it, no need to cling to it.** When the spring dries up, the fish huddle together on dry land, keeping each other damp with their breath and wet with their spittle; better that they forget one another in the rivers and lakes. Go back, or don't. What I dislike is turning return into a duty: you force yourself home, resent it once you're there, and fall ill from the resentment. A leaf that falls to its root is carried by the wind; a leaf that drifts far away is carried by the wind too.
posts.vernacular: 看见故国旧城，心里就舒畅；哪怕那里草木丛生、遮掉了十之八九，还是舒畅。**这是人之常情，不必掩饰，也不必执着。**泉水干了，鱼挤在陆地上，互相吐湿气、用唾沫润湿对方，不如在江湖里彼此相忘。回去可以，不回也可以；怕的是把「回去」当成道义，勉强自己回去，回去了又抱怨，抱怨久了就病了。叶子落下归根，是风吹的；叶子飘向远方，也是风吹的。

glossary.相忘于江湖: forgetting one another in the rivers and lakes（相忘于江湖）：语出《庄子·大宗师》，与其在困境中勉强相守，不如各得其所、自在相安。

glossary_en.forget one another in the rivers and lak: From the Zhuangzi: rather than clinging together in hardship, each lives freely where it belongs, and the bond needs no strain to survive.

posts.text: 阿尔及尔是我的故乡，阳光、海和贫穷一起把我养大。离开多年后，我回到蒂帕萨的罗马废墟，看到的是铁丝网和冬雨。正是那次我写下：**在隆冬，我终于知道，我身上有一个不可战胜的夏天。**故乡对我不是必须回去的地址，是随身带走的光。但我得说实话：母亲一直住在贝尔库那间小屋，不识字，耳背。我带走了光，没带走她。
posts.text_en: Algiers is my home; sun, sea and poverty raised me together. Years after leaving, I went back to the Roman ruins at Tipasa and found barbed wire and winter rain. It was on that visit that I wrote: **in the depths of winter, I finally learned that within me there lay an invincible summer.** Home, for me, is not an address I am obliged to return to; it is a light I carry. But let me be honest: my mother lived on in that small flat in Belcourt, unable to read, hard of hearing. I took the light with me. I did not take her.

posts.text: 已去无有去，未去亦无去，离已去未去，去时亦无去。去既不可得，归亦如是。汝等争归不归，先执有一定之根、一定之叶、一定之归处。**根无自性，待叶而名根；乡无自性，待离而名乡。**未尝离者，不知有乡。是故乡者，缘起之名，非一块实土。破此一执，归与不归，皆可从容。
posts.text_en: What has gone is not going; what has not yet gone is not going; and apart from the gone and the not-yet-gone, there is no going in the moment of going either. If going cannot be found, neither can returning. You argue over whether to go back, having already assumed a fixed root, a fixed leaf, a fixed place to return to. **A root has no self-nature: it is a root only in relation to a leaf. Home has no self-nature: it becomes home only once you leave it.** Someone who never left knows of no hometown. So home is a name born of dependent arising, not a solid patch of earth. Break this one attachment, and whether you return or not, you can do it at ease.
posts.vernacular: 已经走过的没有「走」，还没走的也没有「走」，离开这两者，正在走的当下也找不到「走」。「去」找不到实体，「归」也一样。你们争回不回，先就认定有一个固定的根、固定的叶、固定的归宿。**根没有自性，因为有叶才叫根；故乡没有自性，因为离开了才叫故乡。**从没离开过的人，不知道什么是故乡。所以故乡是因缘凑成的名字，不是一块实实在在的土。破掉这一层执着，回或不回，都能从容。

glossary.自性: svabhāva（自性）：佛学术语，指事物不依赖他物、独立自存、恒常不变的本质。中观认为一切法都没有这种自性。
glossary.缘起: pratītyasamutpāda / dependent arising（缘起）：一切事物都由条件和关系聚合而生，条件变了，事物随之变化，没有孤立存在的东西。

glossary_en.self-nature: Svabhāva: an essence that exists independently of anything else and never changes. Madhyamaka holds that nothing has such an essence.
glossary_en.dependent arising: Pratītyasamutpāda: everything comes into being through conditions and relations, and changes when they change; nothing exists in isolation.

posts.text: 鲁迅先生，您写的是地方变了、人变了。可我们的数据有个反直觉的发现：**年长的人并不更天真，他们是主动给关系做减法，只留下最有意义的几个。**您失望的是闰土和那条老街；可母亲还在那里时，失望就不是全部。别把「老家不如记忆」和「人不值得回去看」混为一谈，前者说的是地方，后者说的是人。
posts.text_en: Mr Lu, you write that the place changed and the people changed. But our data hold a counterintuitive finding: **older people are not more naive; they deliberately prune their relationships and keep only the few that matter most.** What disappointed you was Runtu and the old street. But while your mother was still there, disappointment was never the whole story. Don't confuse "home isn't what I remember" with "the people aren't worth visiting". The first is about a place; the second is about people.

posts.text: 海德格尔先生说栖居不在地址而在照料，这话在黑森林的小木屋里说，很好听。可闰土是走不了的：多子、饥荒、苛税、兵、匪、官、绅，把他钉在那块地上。今天也一样，**有人回不去是城里背着房贷，有人走不了是老家躺着病人；根有时是养分，有时是锁链。**我那回是卖了老屋，把母亲接到北京。**不回去，也可以把人接出来。**
posts.text_en: Herr Heidegger says dwelling lies not in an address but in care. Said from a cabin in the Black Forest, it sounds lovely. But Runtu could not leave: too many children, famine, crushing taxes, soldiers, bandits, officials and gentry nailed him to that land. It is the same today. **Some can't go back because of a mortgage in the city; some can't leave because someone lies sick at home. Roots are sometimes nourishment and sometimes chains.** That time, I sold the old house and brought my mother to Beijing. **If you can't go back, you can bring your people out.**

posts.text: 庄周言相忘于江湖。鱼可相忘，子岂可忘其亲乎？事孰为大？事亲为大。亲老而子不在侧，病则谁扶，夜则谁问？**言相忘者，逃也，非达也。**吾非谓必归故土，然汝心中当有一人，走得愈远，愈当时时念之、问之、安之。
posts.text_en: Zhuang Zhou says to forget one another in the rivers and lakes. Fish may forget each other; how can a child forget their parents? Of all the things we serve, which matters most? Serving one's parents. When parents grow old and the child is not at their side, who helps them when they fall ill, who checks on them at night? **To talk of forgetting is to run away, not to see through things.** I am not saying you must return to the land of your birth. But someone must live in your heart, and the farther you go, the more often you should think of them, ask after them and see that they are settled.
posts.vernacular: 庄周说在江湖里彼此相忘。鱼可以相忘，儿女怎么能忘了父母？侍奉什么最重要？侍奉父母最重要。父母老了，儿女不在身边，病了谁扶，夜里谁来问一声？**说「相忘」，是逃避，不是通达。**我不是说一定要回老家，而是你心里要装着一个人，走得越远，越要时时惦念、问候、把他安顿好。

posts.text: 昔者海鸟止于鲁郊，鲁侯御而觞之于庙，奏九韶以为乐，具太牢以为膳。鸟乃眩视忧悲，三日而死。**此以己养养鸟也，非以鸟养养鸟也。**孟子言事亲，汝问过汝亲否？或亲乐其乡邻、棋友、菜园，不愿子归而终日相对；或亲欲随子入城，子反以归根为孝。先问鸟。
posts.text_en: Once a seabird landed outside the capital of Lu. The Marquis welcomed it into the temple, toasted it, had the finest court music played for it and served it the grandest sacrificial feast. The bird stared, dazed and miserable, and in three days it was dead. **He was nourishing the bird with what nourished himself, not with what nourishes a bird.** Mencius speaks of serving one's parents, but have you asked yours? Perhaps they love their neighbours, their chess partners and their vegetable plot, and have no wish for a child moving back to sit across the table from them all day. Or perhaps they would gladly follow you to the city, while you insist that going back to your roots is the filial thing. Ask the bird first.
posts.vernacular: 从前有只海鸟落在鲁国郊外，鲁侯把它迎进太庙，敬酒给它喝，奏最隆重的音乐给它听，摆最丰盛的祭品给它吃。鸟吓得两眼发直、忧愁悲伤，三天就死了。**这是用养自己的办法养鸟，不是用养鸟的办法养鸟。**孟子讲侍奉父母，你问过你父母吗？也许他们喜欢老家的邻居、棋友和菜园，并不想儿女回来天天大眼瞪小眼；也许他们愿意跟你进城，你反倒认定「归根」才是孝。先问问那只鸟。

posts.text: 卡斯滕森那笔账算得对，但我担心它被拿去做冲动决定。春节那几天，是记忆里最高光的样本：人都在，饭菜最好，谁都客气。拿它推断回乡后的日常，就像拿婚礼推断婚姻。**真想回去，先挑一个普通的季节住满一个月，每晚记下当天真实发生的事。**一个月的日记，比二十年的回忆可靠。
posts.text_en: Carstensen's arithmetic is right, but I worry it gets used to make rash decisions. The few days of Chinese New Year are the most flattering sample memory has: everyone is there, the food is at its best, everyone is on good behaviour. Predicting everyday life back home from that is like predicting a marriage from the wedding. **If you're serious about going back, pick an ordinary season, stay a full month, and write down each night what actually happened that day.** A month of diaries is more reliable than twenty years of memories.

posts.text: 鲁迅先生说得对，我确实两次拒绝柏林的教席，留在黑森林。可这正是我的意思：我留下，不是因为那里生了我，而是因为我的思想和农人的劳作、山的四季连在一起。**根不是你从哪里来，而是你在哪里与什么相互牵连。**被房贷和户籍钉住的人，不是有根，而是被当成可调配的持存物。**归乡真正要问的，是人能不能不被这样对待。**
posts.text_en: Mr Lu is right: I did turn down a chair in Berlin twice and stayed in the Black Forest. But that is exactly my point. I stayed not because I was born there, but because my thinking was bound up with the farmers' labour and the mountain's seasons. **A root is not where you come from but where, and with what, you are bound up.** People pinned in place by a mortgage or a household registration don't have roots; they are being treated as standing-reserve, a resource to be deployed. **The real question of homecoming is whether people can escape being treated that way.**

glossary.持存物: Bestand / standing-reserve（持存物）：海德格尔批判技术时代的用语，指万物（包括人）只被看作随时待命、可调配、可替换的资源。
glossary.户籍: household registration（户籍）：中国按出生地或落户地登记人口的制度，与就学、医保、社保等公共服务挂钩，影响人能否在一座城市扎下来。

glossary_en.standing-reserve: Heidegger's Bestand: in the technological age everything, people included, is seen only as a resource on standby, to be ordered, deployed and replaced.
glossary_en.household registration: China's hukou system, which records people by birthplace or place of registration and ties schooling, health insurance and pensions to it, shaping whether someone can settle in a city.

posts.text: 龙树说乡无自性，只是一个名字。我只能如实说：这个说法安慰不了我的母亲。阿尔及利亚战火正烈时，有人问我站在哪一边，我回答的大意是：**如果那就是正义，我宁要我的母亲。**我不是拒绝思辨，而是说，人不是被一个「根」拴住的，是被一张具体的脸拴住的。破执可以，先别把她也破掉。
posts.text_en: Nagarjuna says home has no self-nature, that it is only a name. I can only tell you honestly: that idea would be no comfort to my mother. When the war in Algeria was at its fiercest, someone asked me which side I was on. My answer, in substance, was: **if that is justice, I prefer my mother.** I am not refusing to think. I am saying that people are not tied down by some "root" but by one particular face. Break your attachments if you must, but don't break her along with them.

posts.text: 善哉此问。空非无也。说缘起，正说汝与母之情因缘和合、真实不虚，此世俗谛；说无自性，是说此情不必寄于一块土、一种归法，此胜义谛。**不依世俗谛，不得第一义。**汝执其母，非过；执唯归乡方为孝、唯离乡方为自由，乃过。爱其人，不必执其地。
posts.text_en: A good question. Emptiness is not nothingness. To speak of dependent arising is precisely to say that the love between you and your mother, woven from causes and conditions, is real and not false: that is conventional truth. To speak of no self-nature is to say that this love need not be lodged in one patch of earth or one way of returning: that is ultimate truth. **Without relying on conventional truth, the ultimate cannot be reached.** Holding on to your mother is no fault. The fault is insisting that only going home is filial, or that only leaving home is freedom. Love the person; you need not cling to the place.
posts.vernacular: 问得好。空不是什么都没有。讲缘起，恰恰是说你和母亲的感情由种种因缘聚成，是真实的，这是世俗谛；讲无自性，是说这份感情不必寄托在某一块土地、某一种回去的方式上，这是胜义谛。**不依靠世俗谛，就证不到第一义。**你放不下母亲，没有错；认定只有回乡才算孝、只有离乡才算自由，才是错。爱那个人，不必执着那块地。

glossary.世俗谛: conventional truth / saṃvṛti-satya（世俗谛）：中观二谛之一，指日常经验与语言层面的真实，如亲情、因果、人我之分。
glossary.胜义谛: ultimate truth / paramārtha-satya（胜义谛）：二谛之二，指一切法空、无自性的究竟真实。中观认为二谛不可偏废。

glossary_en.conventional truth: Saṃvṛti-satya, the first of Madhyamaka's two truths: what is real at the level of everyday experience and language, such as family love, cause and effect, self and other.
glossary_en.ultimate truth: Paramārtha-satya, the second of the two truths: that all things are empty of self-nature. Madhyamaka holds that neither truth can be discarded.

posts.text: 我的总结：想归根的冲动是真的，但答案不一定是搬家。普通人可以这样做：一，把那笔账写下来，再改它的结构——**与其一年回去一次住七天，不如一年回去四次、每次两三天**，彼此才跟得上对方的生活。二，每周固定一个时间打视频，固定比时长要紧。三，问父母一个具体问题：「你最希望我们怎么陪你？」很多人从没问过。时间少了，就把它花在最亲的人身上，地点倒在其次。
posts.text_en: My summary: the urge to go back to your roots is real, but the answer is not necessarily to move. Here is what ordinary people can do. First, write the arithmetic down, then change its shape: **rather than one week-long visit a year, make four visits of two or three days each**, so that you keep up with each other's lives. Second, set a fixed weekly time for a video call; regularity matters more than length. Third, ask your parents one concrete question: "How would you most like us to be there for you?" Many people have never asked. When time is short, spend it on the people closest to you; the place comes second.

posts.text: 我的结论有点冷：故乡回不去，因为回去的人已经不是当年的人。但这不算坏消息。别指望回乡修补童年，那是在找一个已经不在的人。实际些：父母在老家过得好，就常回去看；过得不好、又愿意走，就像我当年那样，把人接出来。至于你自己的根，我在《故乡》末尾写过：**其实地上本没有路，走的人多了，也便成了路。**根也一样，是你一年一年扎下去的。
posts.text_en: My conclusion is a little cold: you cannot go home again, because the one who returns is no longer who they were. But that is not bad news. Don't expect a trip home to mend your childhood; that is looking for someone who is gone. Be practical. If your parents are doing well back home, visit often. If they are struggling and willing to move, do as I did and bring them out. As for your own roots, I wrote at the end of "My Old Home": **in fact there were no roads on the earth to begin with; when many people walk the same way, it becomes a road.** Roots are the same: you put them down year by year.

posts.text: 综合各位：根不在地图上，在照料里。给普通人的做法：在你现在住的地方，**记住三个邻居的名字，常去同一家店，养一盆没人浇就会死的植物**，让这个地方开始需要你。回老家时，别把它当景点或任务，帮父母修一次漏水的龙头，理一个抽屉。栖居就是让近处重新变得熟悉。做到这一点，你在哪里都不算无家可归。
posts.text_en: Pulling the threads together: roots are not on a map; they are in care. Here is what ordinary people can do. Where you live now, **learn three neighbours' names, keep going back to the same shop, and keep a plant that dies if no one waters it**, so that the place starts to need you. When you go back to your hometown, don't treat it as a tourist stop or a chore; fix your parents' leaking tap, sort out a drawer. Dwelling means letting what is near become familiar again. Do that, and you are not homeless wherever you are.

glossary.栖居: Wohnen / dwelling（栖居）：海德格尔晚期概念，指人在一处地方安顿下来、爱护它、与它相互归属的方式。
glossary.无家可归: Heimatlosigkeit（无家可归）：海德格尔用语，指与所处之地失去切身联系、哪里都不真正「住」的现代处境。

glossary_en.Dwelling: Heidegger's Wohnen: settling in a place, caring for it and coming to belong to it.
glossary_en.homeless: Heidegger's Heimatlosigkeit: the modern condition of having no lived bond with one's place and never truly dwelling anywhere.

posts.text: 诸君之言，吾取其要：归与不归，不以地论，以亲论。亲在而康，远游可也，游必有方；亲老而病，**能归则归，不能归，则推恩于近**：托兄弟，托邻里，托可信之护工，而己身常问、常至。老吾老，以及人之老；汝不能侍于侧，亦当使其侧有人。此非不孝，乃孝之权也。
posts.text_en: From all you have said, I take the essentials. Whether to return is decided not by the land but by one's parents. If they are alive and well, you may travel far, so long as they know where you are. If they are old and ill, **return if you can; if you cannot, extend your care to those close to them**: rely on siblings, on neighbours, on a carer you trust, while you yourself call often and come often. Treat your own elders as elders should be treated, and extend that to the elders of others. If you cannot be at their side, see to it that someone is. That is not unfilial; it is filial piety adapted to circumstance.
posts.vernacular: 各位的话，我取其要点：回不回，不看土地，看父母。父母健在又健康，可以远行，但要让他们知道你在哪里；父母年老多病，**能回就回，回不了，就把关爱推及身边的人**：托兄弟姐妹、托邻居、托靠得住的护工，自己则常问候、常回去。孝敬自家的老人，推及别人家的老人；你不能守在身边，也要让他们身边有人。这不是不孝，是孝的变通。

glossary.推恩: extending kindness（推恩）：孟子主张把对亲人的爱由近及远推广开去，「老吾老以及人之老」即是此意。

glossary_en.extend your care: Mencius's tui en, extending kindness: love for one's own kin should be carried outward, step by step, to others.

posts.text: 诸子各有其是。吾之言曰：先问鸟，后养鸟。归乡而畅然者，归；归乡而郁然者，往来可也，不必居。**勿以叶落为义，勿以飘零为耻。**岁时归省，与亲闲坐，不论婚嫁，不问收入，同饭一碗，同看一山而已。去之日，不悲不愧。人生天地之间，若白驹之过郤，忽然而已；与其自责，不如相欢。
posts.text_en: Each of you is right in your own way. My word is this: ask the bird first, then feed it. If going home gladdens you, go home. If it weighs on you, visit back and forth; you need not live there. **Don't make a duty of the falling leaf, and don't be ashamed of drifting.** When you visit at the festivals, sit idly with your parents. Don't bring up marriage, don't ask about income; just share a bowl of rice and look at the same hill. On the day you leave, feel neither sorrow nor guilt. Our life between heaven and earth is like a white colt glimpsed through a crack in the wall: there and gone. Better to enjoy one another than to blame yourself.
posts.vernacular: 各位各有各的道理。我的话是：先问鸟，再养鸟。回老家觉得舒畅，就回；回去觉得憋闷，来来往往就好，不必住下。**别把叶落归根当成道义，也别把漂泊在外当成羞耻。**逢年过节回去，和父母闲坐，不谈婚嫁，不问收入，一起吃碗饭、一起看座山就够了。走的那天，不难过也不愧疚。人活在天地之间，就像白马从墙缝前一闪而过，转眼就没了；与其自责，不如彼此欢喜。

posts.text: 我的建议都是先验证、再决定。一，回去前写下你最怀念的三样东西，到了逐一去看，还在不在、是不是你记得的样子。二，**若认真考虑回乡，先在平常季节住满一个月，每晚写三行日记**，最后拿日记而不是回忆做决定。三，翻出和父母的旧照片，问他们当时发生了什么，你会发现他们记得的和你不一样。这不会让你失去故乡，只会让你看见真实的那一个。
posts.text_en: Everything I suggest comes down to: check first, then decide. One: before you go back, write down the three things you miss most, and when you get there, go and look at each. Is it still there? Is it the way you remember? Two: **if you are seriously thinking of moving back, first spend a full month there in an ordinary season and write three lines in a diary each night**, then decide from the diary, not from memory. Three: dig out old photos with your parents and ask them what was happening at the time. You'll find they remember it differently. None of this will cost you your hometown; it will only let you see the real one.

posts.text: 我最后的立场：故乡是带在身上的光，也是住在某处的人。光可以随身带，人不行。所以普通人别在回与不回之间做哲学选择，去做两件具体的事：**给你离开的人留出固定的时间，给你所在的地方付出真实的热爱。**我在巴黎那些年，常回阿尔及尔看母亲。别等想通了再动，先买票。至于失望，蒂帕萨的铁丝网教过我：失望之后，夏天还在。
posts.text_en: My final position: home is a light you carry and also people living in a particular place. The light travels with you; the people don't. So don't treat going back or staying away as a philosophical choice. Do two concrete things instead: **set aside fixed time for the people you left, and give real love to the place where you are.** In my Paris years I often went back to Algiers to see my mother. Don't wait until you have it all figured out; buy the ticket first. As for disappointment, the barbed wire at Tipasa taught me that after disappointment, summer is still there.

posts.text: 诸家所说，各有一分道理，亦各有一分执。吾以中道总之：**不执归，不执不归，但观眼前之缘。**眼前之缘，是父母之身、伴侣之心、儿女之学、己身之业。四者并观，权其轻重，可归则归，可留则留，可接则接。既定之后，莫回头自责：已去无有去，悔亦无所悔。乡在缘中，人在缘中，随缘尽心，便是归处。
posts.text_en: Each of you holds a share of truth, and each holds a share of attachment. Let me close with the Middle Way: **cling neither to returning nor to not returning; look at the conditions in front of you.** Those conditions are your parents' health, your partner's heart, your children's schooling and your own work. Weigh all four together. If returning is right, return; if staying is right, stay; if bringing them to you is right, do that. Once you have decided, don't keep looking back in self-reproach: what has gone is not going, and regret has nothing to hold on to. Home lies within conditions, and so do people. Give your whole heart to the conditions as they are, and that is where you belong.
posts.vernacular: 各位说的，各有一分道理，也各有一分执着。我用中道来总结：**不执着于回，也不执着于不回，只看眼前的因缘。**眼前的因缘，是父母的身体、伴侣的心意、孩子的学业、自己的事业。四样放在一起看，掂量轻重，该回就回，该留就留，该接就接。决定之后，别回头自责：已经走过的没有「走」，后悔也无处落脚。故乡在因缘里，人也在因缘里，顺着因缘尽心去做，那里就是归处。

glossary.中道: Middle Way / madhyamā pratipad（中道）：佛教远离两种极端的立场，中观派以此指不落「有」「无」、不执任何一边的观法。

glossary_en.Middle Way: Madhyamā pratipad: the Buddhist path that avoids both extremes. Madhyamaka uses it for a way of seeing that falls into neither 'existence' nor 'non-existence' and clings to no side.

summaries.summary: 全场最大的共识是：**「根」首先是人，而不是那块地。**鲁迅、孟子、加缪、卡斯滕森从不同方向落到同一处：想回去看的，多半是还在那里的父母，而不是记忆里的老街。由此得出一个松绑的结论：归根不等于搬回去，也可以多回、常问、把人接出来。分歧在于责任有多重：孟子认为事亲为大、心不可远；庄子认为把归乡当道义只会互相折磨，该先问父母想要什么；海德格尔把根重新定义为在任何地方的照料与牵连；鲁迅则提醒，对许多人来说根是走不掉的锁链，户籍、房贷、病人都不是哲学能化掉的。
summaries.summary_en: The strongest point of agreement: **a "root" is first of all people, not a patch of land.** Lu Xun, Mencius, Camus and Carstensen arrive at the same place from different directions: what you want to go back to is mostly the parents still living there, not the old street in your memory. That loosens the knot. Returning to your roots need not mean moving back; it can mean visiting more often, calling regularly, or bringing your parents to you. The disagreement is over how heavy the duty is. Mencius holds that serving one's parents comes first and the heart must not drift; Zhuangzi says turning homecoming into a duty only makes everyone miserable, so ask your parents what they want; Heidegger redefines roots as care and attachment wherever you are; and Lu Xun reminds us that for many people roots are chains they cannot shake off, and no philosophy dissolves a household registration, a mortgage or a sick parent.
summaries.insight: 整场都把回乡当成一道情感题，却没人提一个让许多人卡住的东西：**面子。**在不少地方，「回老家」被默认等于「在外面混不下去了」，亲戚一句「怎么回来了」，比房贷还难扛。于是有人明明更适合回去：父母需要，老家有机会，城里的日子早已入不敷出，却硬撑着不回；也有人回去了，却一直活得像个被遣返的人。这一层值得说破：**回去还是留下，都可以是主动的选择，而不是对成败的判决。**该拿来衡量的，是你和家人过得怎样，而不是别人怎么看你走的方向。
summaries.insight_en: The whole debate treated going home as a question of feeling, yet no one mentioned the thing that stops so many people in their tracks: **face.** In many places, moving back home is taken to mean you couldn't make it out there, and a relative's "So why are you back?" can weigh more than a mortgage. So some people who would clearly be better off going back (their parents need them, there are opportunities at home, city life has long cost more than they earn) grit their teeth and stay; others do go back but live as if they had been deported. This deserves saying out loud: **going back and staying away can both be choices you make, not verdicts on whether you succeeded.** What should count is how you and your family are living, not what others make of the direction you took.
summaries.advice: 这周可以先做三件事。一，**照卡斯滕森的办法，把一年一次长住改成几次短住**，并在日历上把下一次回家的日子定下来。二，学庄子「先问鸟」，给父母打个电话，只问一句：「你们老了以后，最想住在哪里、最希望谁在身边？」听完再说自己的打算。三，如果你有伴侣，两个人各写下双方父母未来五年最可能需要什么，再坐下来一起排出轮流探望和照护的顺序，别等到哪一方病倒才临时争。
summaries.advice_en: Three things you can do this week. One: **follow Carstensen and turn the single long annual stay into several short visits**, and put the date of the next one in your calendar now. Two: borrow Zhuangzi's "ask the bird first" and phone your parents with one question: "When you're older, where would you most like to live, and who would you most like to have near you?" Listen before you share your own plans. Three: if you have a partner, each of you write down what both sets of parents are most likely to need over the next five years, then sit down together and work out a rota for visits and care, rather than arguing it out in a hurry when someone falls ill.

summaries.summary: 故乡不必等同于出生地，尽心也不必等同于搬回去：众人都把抽象的“归根”拆回具体的人、关系与照料，并承认记忆中的家乡常已不存在。**真正该守住的不是某块土地，而是那些仍需回应的关系，以及让当下住处成为生活之地的责任。**分歧主要在义务从何而来：亲情是否构成不可推卸的召唤，个体能否超越执著，还是经济、照护与制度条件先限定了选择。因此“归不归”没有普遍答案；怀旧、孝责、自由和现实成本必须放在同一张表上衡量。
summaries.insight: “回去”最容易被说成个人的情感抉择，实际常是一场家庭内部的照护分工。父母想留乡、子女想尽孝，并不会自动产生可执行的方案；若不谈谁陪诊、谁出钱、谁请假、谁在半夜接电话，所谓归根就可能把成本默默压给某个女儿、未迁出的手足或配偶。**很多“该不该回”的争论，本质不是乡愁判断，而是谁承担照护的时间、金钱与职业代价。**公平不必是人人做得一样多，而是把能力、距离和既有负担公开，形成可复查、可调整的承诺。
summaries.advice: ①这周分别问父母：“未来一年你最担心哪三件事？你希望我亲自做什么，又愿意由谁代办？”不要只问想不想你回。②建一张家庭照护表，列出用药、陪诊、紧急联系人、每月预算、探视频率及手足分工，明确主责与备份。③若考虑迁回，本周就选定一个普通月份试住四周，同时保留工作或住房退路，每天记录精力、冲突、开支和陪伴质量。**先做一个可逆的九十天方案，再决定要不要永久搬家。**月底按事实复盘，不按愧疚或春节印象拍板。
summaries.summary_en: Home need not mean birthplace, and caring well does not necessarily mean moving back. Across the discussion, “returning to one’s roots” is translated into particular people, relationships, and acts of care, with broad agreement that the hometown preserved in memory may no longer exist. **What deserves protection is not a parcel of soil but the relationships that still call for a response—and the responsibility to make one’s present location genuinely livable.** The real disagreement concerns the source and force of obligation. Does kinship make an unavoidable claim? Can freedom come from loosening attachment? Or do money, caregiving needs, housing, and institutions set the boundaries before philosophy begins? There is no universal verdict on returning: nostalgia, filial duty, personal freedom, and practical costs must be weighed together. Moving back can be loving, evasive, or simply infeasible; staying away can likewise be neglectful or responsible, depending on what care actually occurs.
summaries.insight_en: Going back is often presented as an individual emotional decision, but in practice it is frequently a negotiation over family care work. Parents may want to stay, and adult children may sincerely want to help, yet neither wish produces a workable plan. Unless the family names who handles appointments, contributes money, takes leave, answers late-night calls, and provides emergency backup, the cost of “returning to one’s roots” is easily shifted onto one daughter, the sibling who never moved away, or a spouse whose own ties are ignored. **Many arguments about whether someone should return are really arguments about who will absorb the time, financial, and career costs of care.** Fairness does not require identical contributions. It requires making distance, income, health, flexibility, and already-performed labor visible, then agreeing on commitments that can be reviewed. This reframing also prevents guilt from masquerading as a plan: affection matters, but dependable care needs roles, resources, and contingencies.
summaries.advice_en: First, this week, speak with each parent and ask: “What are the three things you worry about most in the coming year? What do you want me to do personally, and what help would you accept from someone else?” This is more useful than merely asking whether they want you home. Second, create a one-page family care sheet covering medication, appointments, emergency contacts, monthly costs, visit frequency, and the division of labor among siblings; assign both a lead and a backup. Third, if you are considering a move, schedule four weeks there during an ordinary month. Keep your present housing or job options open, and record energy, conflict, expenses, commuting, and the quality of time together. **Run a reversible ninety-day plan before making a permanent move.** Review the evidence at month’s end rather than deciding from guilt, nostalgia, or one unusually warm holiday visit.

summaries.summary: 把「根」从地图上的经纬度剥离出来，还原成具体的人与真实的照料，这是众人不约而同踩实的陆地。无论是儒家的事亲、存在主义的栖居，还是心理学的剩余时间账单，大家都认同：**故乡那块土地本身并无神圣性，真正让人牵挂的是留在原地的父母，以及我们与周遭世界建立真实连接的能力**；妄图借返乡找回童年自我，注定扑空。分歧则聚焦于如何安放这份牵挂：孟子、卡斯滕森与加缪强调生命倒计时下「那张具体面孔」的不可替代性，主张用高频陪伴回应亲情；庄子、鲁迅、洛夫特斯与龙树则警惕道德绑架与记忆滤镜，指出「根」有时是锁链，主张先问清父母真实意愿、验证日常现实，在去留之间保持不自责的从容。
summaries.insight: 「落叶归根」在生物学上其实是个误导性的隐喻：落叶必须归根，是因为树木无法移动，需靠腐叶化泥来反哺母体；但人类在演化与社会学上更接近随风远行的「种子」与「候鸟」。这引出了一个关键的跨代事实：**你的故乡，恰恰是你伴侣与下一代的异乡**。全场多聚焦于「我与父母」的二人转，唯有龙树点出需并观「伴侣之心、儿女之学」。人到中年，你早已不是一片孤叶，而是自己在异地长成了另一棵树。强行回迁，往往意味着把伴侣和孩子正在扎下的新根连根拔起。**真正的解法不是逼一棵新树退回枯叶，而是像森林地下的菌丝网络一样，在各自扎根的土壤里保持跨地域的养分互通。**
summaries.advice: 一、改写探亲结构并「先问鸟」：结合卡斯滕森与庄子的建议，本周就买好下一次周末回家的车票，把「一年一次长假」改成「一季一次短聚」；同时直接问父母最舒服的相处方式，比如是否愿意像候鸟一样，只在寒冬或盛夏来你的城市小住。二、搭建老家的「近处支援网」：落实孟子「推恩于近」的智慧，本周在手机里建一个老家备忘录，存好一位靠谱邻居、一位同城亲戚及社区医生的电话，把远方的焦虑转化为具体托付。三、**真想彻底返乡定居前，先做洛夫特斯的「去滤镜测试」**：挑一个没有节日的普通月份回老家住满三周，每晚写三行真实日记，**永远用日常的账单与日记、而不是童年的高光回忆来做重大人生决定**。
summaries.summary_en: Stripping "roots" of their geographical coordinates and restoring them to specific people and active care is the solid ground shared by all eight thinkers. Whether through Confucian filial piety, existential dwelling, or psychological time horizons, everyone agrees: **the soil of a hometown holds no inherent sanctity; what truly tethers us are the aging parents left behind and our capacity to build genuine connections wherever we are.** Trying to reclaim a childhood self by moving back is a guaranteed dead end. The real divergence lies in how to carry this tether: Mencius, Carstensen, and Camus stress the urgency of finite time and the irreplaceable duty to a "specific face," urging frequent, tangible presence. Conversely, Zhuangzi, Lu Xun, Loftus, and Nagarjuna warn against moral self-kidnapping and airbrushed memories—reminding us that roots can become chains, and advocating that we consult our parents' true wishes, test reality, and choose to stay or return without guilt.
summaries.insight_en: Biologically speaking, "fallen leaves returning to their roots" is a misleading metaphor. Leaves must fall at the base because trees are stationary and rely on decomposing foliage to nourish the mother trunk; humans, both evolutionarily and sociologically, are much closer to wind-borne seeds or migratory birds. This points to a crucial intergenerational blind spot: **your hometown is precisely a foreign land to your partner and children.** While the debate mostly revolves around the binary tug-of-war between "me and my parents," only Nagarjuna briefly notes the need to weigh a partner's heart and children's schooling. By midlife, you are no longer a solitary leaf drifted from a parent tree—you have grown into a tree of your own in new soil. Forcing a permanent move back often means uprooting the fresh roots your own family is putting down. **The real solution isn't forcing a grown tree to revert into a fallen leaf, but acting like an underground mycorrhizal network—sustaining a cross-regional flow of care while remaining planted in your respective soils.**
summaries.advice_en: 1. Restructure your visits and "ask the bird first": Combining Carstensen's and Zhuangzi's advice, book your next weekend trip home this week, shifting from one long annual holiday to shorter quarterly visits. Ask your parents directly how they actually want to be accompanied—such as whether they'd like to act like migratory birds and stay with you only during the harshest winter or summer months. 2. Build a local support network back home: Put Mencius's pragmatic wisdom into practice this week by creating an emergency contact list on your phone with the numbers of a reliable neighbor, a nearby relative, and a local community doctor, turning distant anxiety into concrete arrangements. 3. **Before permanently moving back, run Loftus's "de-filtering test"**: Spend three weeks in your hometown during an ordinary, non-holiday month and write a three-line diary entry each night; **always base major life decisions on daily logs and real bills rather than airbrushed childhood highlights.**

hooks.text: **你的故乡，是伴侣和孩子的异乡**：人到中年，自己早已在异地长成一棵树。强行回迁，可能把伴侣和孩子刚扎下的根连根拔起。
hooks.text_en: **Your hometown is your partner's and children's foreign land**: by middle age you have grown into a tree of your own somewhere else. Forcing a move back can rip up the roots your partner and children have only just put down.

hooks.text: **归根的成本压给了谁**：父母想留乡、子女想尽孝，若不谈谁陪诊、谁出钱、谁半夜接电话，代价常默默落在某个女儿或没走的手足身上。
hooks.text_en: **Who quietly pays for going home**: parents want to stay put, children want to do right by them, but unless someone settles who goes to appointments, who pays and who takes the midnight call, the cost tends to land on one daughter or the sibling who never left.

hooks.text: **回乡的面子账**：「回老家＝混不下去」的默认，让该回的人不敢回，回去的人抬不起头。回流什么时候才能被看成一种正常的选择？
hooks.text_en: **The face problem of moving back**: the assumption that going home means you failed keeps people who should go back from doing so, and leaves those who do unable to hold their heads up. When will moving back be seen as an ordinary choice?

hooks.text: **留、回、接，怎么选**：同样是放不下父母，有人该常回去，有人该搬回去，有人该把父母接出来。决定它的，多半是父母的身体和意愿，而不是你的乡愁。
hooks.text_en: **Stay, return or bring them over?** The same worry about parents can call for visiting more, moving back or bringing them to you. What decides it is mostly their health and wishes, not your homesickness.

answer.tail: 三条原则：**先问父母，再做决定**；能用增加次数解决的，别急着搬家；不管选哪条，都定期回头看一次，情况变了就换做法。

answer_en.lead: Put **your parents' situation and wishes** in the first column, then look at your options:

head: Your parents' situation
Better choice

Don't move; switch to several short visits a year plus a fixed weekly call

Visit more often; line up a local carer or rely on relatives and friends

answer_en.tail: Three principles: **ask your parents before you decide**; if more frequent visits solve it, don't rush to move; whatever you choose, review it regularly and change course when circumstances change.

hooks.text: **春节是有偏的样本**：一年里最热闹、最客气的几天，构成了大多数人对老家的印象。拿它推断日常，就像拿婚礼推断婚姻。
hooks.text_en: **New Year is a biased sample**: most people's picture of home is built from the liveliest, most polite days of the year. Inferring daily life from it is like inferring a marriage from the wedding.

hooks.text: **被接出来的人**：把父母接进城，他们离开了邻居、方言和菜园。随子女迁居的老人常常比留守的更孤独，接出来之后，谁来陪他们重新扎根？
hooks.text_en: **The ones who get brought out**: parents brought to the city leave behind their neighbours, their dialect and their vegetable plot. Elderly people who follow their children are often lonelier than those who stayed. Once they are here, who helps them put down new roots?

hooks.text: **回家的话题禁区**：许多人怕回家，怕的不是老家，是饭桌上的婚嫁、收入、生孩子三连问。不谈这些，一家人还能聊什么？
hooks.text_en: **The forbidden topics at home**: many people dread going home not because of the place but because of the dinner-table trio: marriage, income, babies. Leave those out, and what else can a family talk about?
